children: rose 6% Thursday as investors focused on its Sanand operation in Gujarat, where the memory-chip maker is expanding assembly and testing to serve rising demand for storage and memory tied to AI.

is backed by about $2.75 billion from Micron and government partners. Commercial output began earlier this year, and Micron expects production to reach tens of millions of chips in 2026 before rising to hundreds of millions in 2027.

The site processes DRAM and NAND wafers from Micron's global manufacturing network and converts them into finished memory and storage products. Its first phase is planned to include more than 500,000 square feet of cleanroom space once fully ramped.

Chief Executive Sanjay Mehrotra said Micron plans to increase assembly and test activity at Sanand next year. The India project adds capacity to the company's worldwide assembly and test network and complements planned advanced manufacturing and packaging work in the United States.
Micron's expansion comes as AI infrastructure spending supports demand for higher-capacity memory and storage products.

title: Micron Stock Soars as India Facility Bets Big on AI Memory Demand
